_doc: Known panel-vs-browser differences check.py accepts (format: scripts/screenshots/checks.py). Every entry says why. Measured against main with the browser drawing the panel's Roboto; bounds are the largest offset seen plus a few px. Fixed a gap on the panel? Tighten or delete its entry (check.py lists entries a run didn't need). Never widen an entry to make a PR pass without saying so in the PR.

offsets.reason: Box shape, not position: the rail's name labels are 88 px wide cells with the name centred, the browser box is the name itself (Δx ≈ −(88 − w) / 2, Δw = 88 − w).
Avatar initials: the panel centres one glyph in a label as tall as the avatar's font line; the browser box is the glyph's CSS line box (Δh 8–18 px). The avatars themselves line up.
Tab labels: the panel draws them with the 22 px body font, .dash-tab-label is 20 px (Δw +5–10 %; known gap), so the unread badge after 'Messages' sits 8 px further right.

offsets.text: ^(message for everyone|nachricht an alle|message for you|nachricht für dich)$
offsets.reason: Alert label: .dash-alert-label's letter-spacing makes the panel's label 15–19 px wider; on Mia's page the alert row sits 12 px lower (see the reader entries).

offsets.text: ^(\d+ min ago|vor \d+ min\.|\d+ h ago|vor \d+ std\.)$
offsets.reason: Relative time after the alert's author: follows the alert label's extra width (Δx = the label's Δw); the minute it shows ticks between runs.
The alert's / a message's author name: follows the alert label's extra width (Δx).
Got it button: the panel's button is a few px wider and sits 6 px higher in the alert row.
Box shape: the panel's alert text is a fixed-width label cut with …, the browser box ends at its ellipsis (Δw).
The big clock: .dash-clock is line-height 1 on a 102.4 px font, the panel's label is the 104 px font's own line (Δh −18, Δy +8–12); the digits shown change the width.

Box shape: the who's-where zone label and a today lane's label span their row on the panel, the browser box is the word (Δw; the today lanes' bars grow with the clock); 'Work' (a person on the way) starts after the 30 px car icon on the panel.
Message line with an emoji: the panel splits it into a label per word plus a picture; the run of labels is a few px wider and lower.
Box shape: a wrapped message — the panel label is the full column width and both lines tall, the browser box is the text's lines.
Small labels whose CSS line box and the panel's font line differ by a few px (badges, headings, the date).

Known gap: the Overview's messages card puts a message's NEW badge in the time column in the browser (~83 px left of the edge), at the row's right edge on the panel. Shows only while the seeded message still counts as new.

The today timeline's 'now' marker moves with the clock (~1 px a minute and between refreshes): panel and browser draw it from fetches up to 30 s apart and round its position differently. Seen 9 px apart in CI.

offsets.text: ^(can't reach social home|social home ist nicht erreichbar)
offsets.reason: Box shape: the offline note's label spans the note on the panel, the browser box is the sentence (Δw).
Box shape: the attachment line is a full-width label on the panel, the browser box is the word (Δw).

offsets.text: ^(@mia don't forget your piano book|bins are out\. have a good day)
offsets.reason: Box shape: wrapped / cut message text — the panel label is the column width and every line tall.
Message times and day headings: each message row is up to 13 px taller on the panel (the author line's font line), so later rows drift down a little.
Box shape: a sticky note's text is a label as wide as the note on the panel and as tall as its lines; the browser box is the text (Δw, and Δh where the note wraps by another line).

offsets.text: ^(anna|leo|mia|pascal|a|l|m|p|school|schule|away|unterwegs|home|zuhause|\d+ min ago|vor \d+ min\.|zuletzt gesehen vor \d+ std\.|last seen \d+ h ago)$
offsets.reason: Who's-where list next to the map: rows are 8–14 px taller on the panel, so the list drifts down to 36 px by its last row; the time label spans the row on the panel (Δw).
Heading: font line vs CSS line box.
Known gap: Mia's 'School today' puts the subject beside the time on the panel, under it in the browser — subjects / rooms sit up to 140 px right and their rows end up to 60 px higher.
Lesson times follow the shorter school rows (above); the NOW / NEXT times use a bigger font on the panel; the header clock is bold 48 px on the panel, light 72 px in the browser.

offsets.text: ^(empty dishwasher|· today|· heute|all day|ganztägig|project week|school today|schule heute|today|heute|chores|aufgaben|tomorrow|morgen|dinner with gran|first lesson|erste stunde|now|jetzt|next|danach|school|schule|mia)$
offsets.reason: Mia's page: the NOW / NEXT cards are 10–14 px taller on the panel (bigger fonts), so everything below starts ~22 px lower.
Known gap: Leo's picture view draws the NOW / NEXT cards' words with bigger fonts and centres them differently on the panel, and the day row's tiles have other widths (Swimming sits 70 px off).

offsets.text: ^(tap to show the dashboard|tippen, um das dashboard zu zeigen|wednesday, october \d+|mittwoch, \d+\. oktober)$
offsets.reason: Box shape: the hint's and the date's CSS line boxes are 40 px taller than the panel's font lines (the night layout's big line-height).
Night clock and the 'Tomorrow' line: font line vs CSS line box, the light 200 weight's digits.
Lock screen header: the household name / date labels are a little wider and the date's CSS line box much taller (Δh); with the note shown the header sits up to 12 px lower.
PIN pad keys: the pad starts up to 18 px higher on the panel (the note above it is shorter).
The hint under the pad: follows the pad up and wraps in the panel's fixed width.

offsets.text: ^(wrong pin|falsche pin|tries left: \d+|verbleibende versuche: \d+|last try — one more wrong pin|letzter versuch — noch eine falsche pin)
offsets.reason: Box shape: the wrong-PIN note's lines are labels as wide as the note with the text centred, the browser box is the text (Δx ≈ −Δw / 2).

texts.reason: The browser's lock page has an Unlock submit button for the tablet's form; the panel unlocks from its own PIN button.
The browser renders its PIN pad (hidden behind the summary) on the lock screen already; the panel builds the pad when 'PIN' is tapped.
Zone names on the map are HTML labels in the browser, drawn into the map picture on the panel.
Known gap: the browser's 'My day' row has a fourth, evening tile (Dinner with Gran) the panel leaves out.
The panel's shorter school rows (see offsets) fit two more lessons above the bottom edge.
